name: firewood
_note: fuel; 2 dry sticks also make a fire by friction

actions.label: cook
log: The fish hisses on a flat stone by the fire.
The fish spits and curls on a hot stone.
Fat drips into the embers. The fish browns.
Hot flesh, flaking from the bone.
Hot and soft. You eat it down to the bones.
It burns your fingers. You eat it anyway.
Salty and chewy. Barely a mouthful.
You suck the meat from the shells. Salt, mostly.
Chewy, salty, gone in a moment.

actions.label: cook
log: The shell pops open in the embers.
The shells hiss and crack open in the heat.
Steam, a snap, and the shells open.
Tender and hot. The smell of the sea.
Hot and tender, tasting of the sea.
Soft meat from hot shells. Better cooked.
Sour, then sweet. Your mouth goes purple.
A handful of berries, gone in a moment.
Sharp and sweet. Not much, but something.

name: rock knife
_note: a sharpened stone: sharp like the knife, but everything takes twice as long with it

name: matches
_note: a box of 10 from the shipwreck; light fire uses one

name: water can
_note: stays when the water is gone; 'fill' at a water source you have explored (the spring, the river)

actions.label: fill
log: You hold the can in the spring until it brims.
Cold water gurgles into the can.
You fill the can to the top and screw the lid on tight.

actions.label: fill
log: You hold the can under the river's surface until it stops bubbling.
The current pushes river water into the can.
You fill the can in the river and screw the lid on tight.

name: water in the can

log: You drink from the can. It tastes of tin, but it is water.
A long swallow from the can.
You drink, then screw the lid back on tight.

_note: up to 4 drinks; refilled from the water can's 'fill'

log: Hard biscuit and salt meat, soaked with sea water. Still food.
You chew a ration slowly, making it last.
Salt meat and a damp biscuit. Your stomach is grateful.

name: stones
_note: picked up under the cliff; 2 strike sparks for a fire; for the rock knife, the axe, the hoe and the weir

name: logs
_note: better wood than firewood: chopped in the forest with the axe

name: willow twigs
_note: cut by the river; 20 for a fish trap

name: bark strips
_note: cut from the trees in the forest with something sharp; 4 make a rope

name: rope
_note: twisted from bark strips (craft menu, 3 h); climbs the cliff (kept) and makes snares

name: corn
_note: also the seed for the corn field

log: Hard, starchy kernels. You chew a long time.
Raw corn, tough and faintly sweet.
You gnaw the kernels off the cob.

actions.label: roast
log: You roast the ear in the embers until the kernels split.
The husk blackens; the kernels inside go gold.
Corn in the embers, turned until it smells sweet.
Hot, sweet and smoky.
You eat it off the cob, burning your fingers.
Sweet roasted corn. Real food.
Hard and salty. You tear it with your teeth.
Dry fish, chewy and smoky.
It takes a long time to chew. It fills you.

actions.label: dry
actions.log: You cut two portions of meat into thin strips and hang them on the drying rack.

actions.label: cook
log: Meat on a stick over the fire, dripping into the flames.
The meat spits and browns over the fire.
You turn the meat over the flames until it is brown through.
Tough strips of dried meat. You chew slowly.
Smoky, chewy meat. It fills you.
Hot meat, fat running down your chin.
Rich and hot. The best meal on the island.
You eat slowly. Real meat.
Soft, earthy, a little bitter.
They taste of the forest floor.
Cool and earthy.
Sweet enough to make your eyes water.
Honey and wax and a dead bee. Sweet.
You suck the comb dry.
